name: FormMCP
title: one MCP connection from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor to the whole Form family
summary: FormMCP is the one MCP server you add for the Form family: agents see every FormAI app in one short list and load an app's own tools only when a task needs it.
lede: FormMCP is the one MCP server you add to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor for the Form family of desktop apps. The agent sees every FormAI app in one short list, whether or not any of them is installed, and loads one app's own tools only when the task needs that app. FormMCP suggests; FormPortal installs.
checks: Gives Claude Code, Codex or Cursor every FormAI app in one short list, with no app's tools loaded up front.
Starts one app's own MCP server only when the task needs it, and returns that app's results unchanged.
Lets you turn apps off per agent and single tools off for every agent, and save that as a profile to share.
Keeps secrets in the system keychain, hides token-shaped text, and refuses to start an installed app whose files changed.

facts.dd: Rust (formmcp-core, formmcp-cli) in a Tauri 2 shell, with a vanilla TypeScript and Vite window with zero runtime dependencies
24 FormAI apps from FormCompiler's registry and the signed catalogue, 8 MCP tools, stdio and HTTP, 2 ways to reach an app, 3 agent clients
Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, over stdio or over HTTP on 127.0.0.1:5625 with an access token
nodemode-dev/formMCP; FormMCP is the display name

chapters.title: The whole family in one short list
chapters.text: family_apps returns one line per FormAI app and no app's tools: what each is for, whether it has an MCP server and whether this computer can reach it. That is one line per app, whether or not any of them is installed.

chapters.title: One app's own tools, only when the task needs them
chapters.text: app_tools starts one app's own MCP server, through its checkout's launcher or FormPortal for an install, and lists its tools; call_app runs one and returns the app's result unchanged. Nothing is copied, so the tools are always the running app's.

chapters.title: You choose what each agent gets
chapters.text: Turn an app off for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or other agents, turn single tools off for every agent, and save it as a profile a teammate can import. Off apps leave the lists and are refused with the reason, from the next request.

features.title: Cheap on context
features.text: family_apps returns one line per app and no app's tools, so the whole family stays a short list, not every app's tools loaded up front.
bullets: Each app's id, name, kind, one line on what it is for, whether it has an MCP server and its release state
Whether FormPortal installed it here, and how FormMCP can reach it: dev for a checkout, formportal for an install
mcp_only keeps the apps with an MCP server

features.title: Apps' tools on demand
features.text: app_tools starts one app's own MCP server and lists its tools; call_app runs one and returns the app's result unchanged. Nothing is copied, so the tools are always the running app's.
bullets: Started through the app's checkout launcher, or formportal app-mcp for a FormPortal install
An app that fails to start comes back with its own last output
Always show tools puts one app's tools straight into the tool list, as <id>__<tool>
Off for every app by default, because each exposed app costs its whole tool list in every conversation

features.title: Resources and prompts
features.text: When an app offers documents or prompt templates, four tools pass them through on demand, like its tools.
bullets: app_resources lists an app's resources and resource templates
read_app_resource reads one by its uri
app_prompts lists an app's prompt templates with their arguments
get_app_prompt fills one and returns the app's messages

features.title: Per-agent choices
features.text: Turn an app off for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or other agents, and turn single tools off, say an app's delete, for every agent.
bullets: Off apps leave the lists and are refused with the reason
Changes apply from the next request
The window's Apps for picker and each card's On for switch
./formmcp cli for codex formvis off and ./formmcp cli tool formvis erase_all off

features.title: Profiles you can share
features.text: Save what an agent gets (apps off, tools off, start policies) as a named profile, use it for any agent, and export it as one file for a teammate to import.
bullets: A profile only ever turns more off
Export writes formmcp-profile-<name>.json to Downloads, never over an existing file
Import drops, and names, apps and policies this FormMCP does not know
Another format or a file over 256 KB is refused

features.title: Start policies
features.text: Per app: start on demand and stop after 10 idle minutes, start in the background when an agent's session starts, or keep running while FormMCP runs.
bullets: Start on demand is the default
Start with the session, so the first call does not wait
Keep running holds an app across HTTP sessions
./formmcp cli start <id> demand, session or keep

features.title: Safe by default
features.text: Secrets an app needs live in the system keychain and reach only that app; secrets and token-shaped text are hidden in results and the log.
bullets: Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, the Secret Service over D-Bus on Linux
Only a secret's name is written to settings.json
API keys, access tokens, JWTs, private keys, and password and token assignments are hidden
An installed app whose files changed is refused, checked against FormPortal's SHA-256 record from FormPortal 0.46.0

features.title: Hooks and tracing
features.text: Optional hooks can allow or refuse each app tool call, and optional tracing sends names and outcomes to an OpenTelemetry collector.
bullets: A before hook gets the call as JSON on stdin and can refuse it
A before hook that fails, prints something that is not JSON or takes longer than 10 s refuses the call
An after hook gets the outcome and the cleaned result
Spans and metrics carry names and outcomes only

features.title: stdio or HTTP
features.text: Agents start formmcp mcp, or reach http://127.0.0.1:5625/mcp while the window or formmcp serve is open.
bullets: This computer only, with an access token on every request
Host and Origin checked on every request
The token renewed with one button, New token, or ./formmcp cli http rotate
Streamable HTTP, protocol 2025-06-18, older versions accepted

features.title: The right app for the task
features.text: suggest_app takes the task in the person's words and returns the apps that fit, best first, with the next step.
bullets: Up to five apps, three when no limit is given
Load its tools, install it with FormPortal, or install FormPortal first
Or why an agent cannot drive it yet
It never installs anything

features.title: Never hand-kept
features.text: The family list is the signed family catalogue over a list generated from FormCompiler's registry, and every answer says which one was used and why.
bullets: The catalogue is checked against the same keys FormPortal trusts
FormPortal's kept copy when offline, the built-in list as the fallback
./formmcp family --compiler PATH regenerates the built-in list; --check fails while it drifts
Until the family's catalogue key pair exists, no key is trusted and the built-in list is used

features.title: Suggests, never installs
features.text: FormMCP lists apps and runs their MCP tools. There is no tool that installs, updates or removes an app; the server tells the agent that FormPortal does.
bullets: Tools only: the FormAI apps' released skills are viewed, downloaded and edited in formskills
The Form family only, with no third-party or remote MCP servers
It leaves itself out of its own list, so no agent can start FormMCP inside FormMCP

features.title: Headless first
features.text: The engine and the MCP server need no window. The installed app answers formmcp mcp on stdio without opening one, so it is its own launcher.
bullets: formmcp-core holds the family list and the MCP server; the command line and the shell are thin
./formmcp cli apps prints the family list as JSON
./formmcp cli reach shows how each app's server would be started
On Linux the MCP server and the command line need only libdbus

features.title: A window that does not flicker
features.text: Connect FormMCP to Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with one button each, see every app's install state and how FormMCP reaches it, and watch the activity.
bullets: Each app's card shows whether it is installed, its version and how FormMCP reaches it
Activity shows sessions, tool calls and app starts, never their arguments
A Safety panel for secrets, hiding, the file check, hooks and tracing
Painted complete in its first frame; nothing moves when the live state arrives

requirements: On Linux, libdbus and pkg-config for the system keychain (libdbus-1-dev and pkg-config on Debian or Ubuntu)
On Linux, WebKitGTK 4.1 for the window; the installer prints the packages
docs.run:
./formmcp
./formmcp mcp
./formmcp cli apps
Windows: formmcp.bat, formmcp.bat mcp
docs.agents: ./formmcp cli agents install adds FormMCP to Claude Code, Codex and Cursor for your user account, as Connect does in the window; agents then run formmcp mcp on stdio, or reach http://127.0.0.1:5625/mcp with the access token from ./formmcp cli http token.

topics.title: Getting Started
topics.text: .docs/wiki/Getting-Started.md covers the requirements, running from source, building the desktop app with build_app, refreshing the family list and the ports.

topics.title: Agents
topics.text: .docs/wiki/Agents.md covers connecting Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, the 8 MCP tools, apps per agent, profiles, start policies, HTTP, secrets, hooks, the activity log and the environment variables.

topics.title: Architecture
topics.text: .docs/wiki/Architecture.md describes the engine and its two thin surfaces, the gateway, the catalogue, safety and tracing, the family list and the window.

topics.title: Ports
topics.text: 5620 is the Vite dev server and 5621 its preview, both localhost only; 5625 is FormMCP over HTTP on 127.0.0.1, changed with FORMMCP_HTTP_PORT or http_port in settings.json.

topics.title: Releases
topics.text: FormMCP builds nothing in its own repository: a compile_vX.Y.Z branch cut from main is built by FormCompiler, which drafts the release formMCP-vX.Y.Z.

topics.title: Notices
topics.text: NOTICE.md lists FormMCP's dependencies with their licences, and the crates the desktop shell links under other licences.

items: The installers and the app metadata name NodeAgentc, Inc. as the publisher, with the licence (GPL-3.0-only)
The macOS About panel, the Windows file properties and installer, and the Linux packages say the same
No change to the app itself
The family catalogue is read from https://dl.formai.studio/catalog/apps.json with its signature beside it; FORMMCP_CATALOG still overrides it
This build trusts the family's production catalogue key
Links to the Form repositories point at the nodemode-dev organisation, and the built-in family list now holds 24 apps
A test suite checks the family list and the signed catalogue, which apps this computer can reach, and the MCP server over stdio and over HTTP
It covers the HTTP access token, Host and Origin checks, and that a call to an app that cannot start fails at once with the reason
The suite runs on every change; nothing in the app changes

shots_wanted.what: The main window: Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with their Connect buttons, the HTTP bar, and the Form family list with each app's install state and route
shots_wanted.how: Run ./formmcp_oc_install, then ./formmcp. Keep at least one FormAI app checkout in the folder beside the formMCP checkout so its card shows a route.

shots_wanted.what: One app's Tools panel with its own tools listed and one tool turned off
shots_wanted.how: On the card of an app with an MCP server and a route, press Tools, then Load tools, and switch one tool off.

shots_wanted.what: The family list for one agent, with an app turned off for it
shots_wanted.how: Choose Codex in Apps for, then switch one card's On for Codex off; leave Profile on None.

shots_wanted.what: The Safety panel: secrets, Hide secrets in results, the file check, hooks and tracing
shots_wanted.how: Open Safety in the window. On Linux, keeping a secret needs a running, unlocked Secret Service such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet.

shots_wanted.what: The Activity panel during an agent session
shots_wanted.how: Open Claude Code in the formMCP checkout, which .mcp.json already wires to ./formmcp mcp, ask it which FormAI apps there are, and capture Activity with the session and the family_apps call.
